title: Presbyterian school at Hot Springs and his brother joining the circus
summary: Their mother sent the boys to a parochial school in Hot Springs in 1912; his brother ran off to Ringling Brothers, performing a side-show act with Mantan Moreland.

venues.name: Ringling Brothers and Barnum & Bailey Circus

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yes.
That's when me and my brother got shipped off to Hot Springs to school to the parochial school.
Your mother sent you there?
Yeah, she sent us there. Then we -- Presbyterian school, and then we studied music.
Uh-huh.
And my brother, he stayed at school awhile, so when school was out he didn't come back to school and he didn't come home, so we wondered where was brother. I
wondered where he was. And I was a sick soul. So, here's what happened. He joined Ringling Brothers and Barnum and Bailey's and then one --
Joined them as what -- a musician?

Yeah, he joined the show. And then when we come back -- and so he came back to school one day and everybody was ran to see -- they called him Jonas -- "Here come Jonas, Here's Jonas. Jonas is back." So, he asked Mrs. McBain -- she was assistant principal.
What was her name?

Mrs. McBain, and her husband, Dr. McBain, a doctor of divinity, he was the principal and she was assistant -- man and wife team there at the school. He asked her to let the kids come out to see him at the show. So, they was glad to see Jonas and so she didn't have any school one day. She just let -- that was a free day.
Everybody could go to the circus?
Everybody went to the circus to see Joe. Now --
What was he doing with the circus?
Yeah, now -- he and Mantan had an act --

Moreland
Mantan Mollen --
Yes.
You ever heard of Mantan --
Sure, I saw him many times.
Yes, uh-huh. Well, Mantan and my brother had an act. They was in the side show. And they sang and danced and he's they're still dancing and singing, dancing and singing.
I'll be darned. When was this about?

This was in 1912, 1913, 1914, round about 1914, I believe. Somewhere around (skew) 1914. And while Mantan was up doing his dance my brother -- I was out in the audience andhe saw me, and he held five fingers up there and he took and thumped a nickel out [there]. Yes, we had a wonderful time that evening. I stayed there almost until dark. Yeah.
